transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-30 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Cascade AI CTO), Maya Torres (ML Engineer), Samir Khan (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick discovery - interested in Redwood PLG quickstart, free credits, evaluating hosted first with possible Dedicated POC for latency-sensitive reranker.

[00:00] Jordan Myers: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, with me is Priya our SE. how are you all doing?
[00:06] Alex Chen: Doing well, thanks. I have Maya and Samir with me. we're excited to learn how fast we can get tokens flowing, uh quickstart type stuff.
[00:12] Maya Torres: Yeah we mostly want to validate latency, cost, and data controls.
[00:16] Priya Patel: Awesome. real quick, is the current stack cloud-native? where are your models running today?
[00:22] Samir Khan: We're on aws, a mix: some inference with managed endpoints (not at scale), and some local infra for dev. we've been prototyping with OpenAI for gen features but the reranker is our priority, want to move to a cheaper/closer solution.
[00:35] Jordan Myers: Great makes sense. high level Redwood has three modes: hosted API for fast time-to-value and PLG quickstart (free credits, self-serve), Dedicated reserved capacity for sustained throughput with predictable latency/cost, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for compliance.
[00:52] Alex Chen: Quick question — free credits, does that let us spin up and hit first token within minutes? or are there approvals?
[00:58] Jordan Myers: For PLG quickstart typically you can redeem credits and call the hosted API within minutes. you sign up, get an API key, and you can call with curl or SDK. we also provide templates and a ready-to-run example for reranking so time-to-first-token is usually under 30 minutes for basic test calls.
[01:15] Maya Torres: Nice. what about rate limits and quota? we might need consistent qps for perf tests.
[01:20] Priya Patel: Hosted has tiered quotas and soft limits; for larger throughput we recommend Dedicated — that's reserved GPU pools with autoscaling policies and SLA. for POC we can usually increase quota temporarily or run a dedicated benchmark with SE.
[01:33] Samir Khan: And the dedicated option — how hard is the migration from hosted? like we want same API surface.
[01:39] Jordan Myers: Migration is intended to be near seamless — same API, same model catalog. you can pin model versions and rollouts remain identical. there are some config differences around networking and keys but we help with that during onboarding.
[01:50] Alex Chen: sounds good. security: we have SOC2 plus strict key management policies. can we bring our own KMS and get audit logs?
[01:58] Priya Patel: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS integrations and detailed audit logs. hosted customers can also integrate KMS for encryption-at-rest and we expose audit logs for API calls; Private (VPC) gives you the most control. we can share our SOC2 and ISO docs after the call.
[02:13] Maya Torres: Are there any gotchas around PII/data residency in hosted? we have some european data concerns.
[02:20] Jordan Myers: We support region-based hosting; if you need EU residency we can provision EU region endpoints. for strict residency or air-gapped needs, Private on-prem is the route.
[02:29] Samir Khan: For cost modeling — we do a reranker that does a single pass on 10 results per query, about 200k queries/day. what's the best lever? batching? quantization? cheaper models?
[02:39] Priya Patel: All of the above. Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles and suggest model variants that maintain quality. for reranking you can often use a smaller encoder model for embeddings and then a mid-size for rerank. we can run a unit-cost estimate after you share sample payloads.
[02:52] Alex Chen: On latency we target 50-100ms p50 for rerank. is that achievable on hosted or do we need Dedicated?
[02:59] Priya Patel: 50ms p50 is aggressive for some models on shared hosted infrastructure depending on token lengths and qps. Dedicated with pinned GPUs and tuned runtimes gives more predictable p50. we should run a dedicated latency benchmark — we do that in the POC.
[03:12] Jordan Myers: also worth noting kernel selection and continuous batching in our runtime optimizes for seq length distribution — that'll help.
[03:20] Maya Torres: ok cool. what does the POC timeline look like?
[03:24] Jordan Myers: Typically: quickstart (self-serve) day 0-1 to validate flows and calls using free credits; SE-led benchmark within 1-2 weeks to validate latency/throughput on Dedicated, and then decision on reserved capacity or Private if required.
[03:36] Samir Khan: Who owns the benchmark?
[03:38] Priya Patel: We do — Priya will run it with you: we'll need sample payloads, expected QPS, and your success criteria. we'll share a spreadsheet and test harness.
[03:47] Alex Chen: Great. a couple more compliance questions: SSO/SAML? RBAC? can we limit team access and integrate with our IdP?
[03:55] Jordan Myers: Yes, enterprise plans support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC. we also support fine-grained role controls in the console.
[04:04] Maya Torres: Are there limits on model variants for Dedicated? like can we bring a custom model or fine-tuned checkpoint?
[04:10] Priya Patel: You can bring custom models for Dedicated and Private — we support model onboarding and can run compatibility/quantization passes. for hosted we have a curated catalog, but we also support customer model hosting on Dedicated/Private.
[04:22] Samir Khan: Any notes on telemetry and cost breakdown? we want token-level cost and per-route breakdowns.
[04:27] Jordan Myers: Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks. we can increase retention or provide exports for chargeback.
[04:35] [brief cross talk, inaudible]
[04:40] Alex Chen: ok can you share the quickstart link and the tutorial for reranker?
[04:44] Jordan Myers: Absolutely — I'll send the quickstart repo, a pre-built rerank example, and the free credits redemption steps.
[04:50] Priya Patel: we'll also include step-by-step for a cURL call, python SDK snippet, and a sample request/response for your scenario.
[04:58] Maya Torres: nice. for the dedicated POC, do you provide compute or do we bring infra?
[05:03] Priya Patel: For Dedicated POC we provide the capacity as part of the trial in most cases; if you prefer on-prem or VPC peering we can coordinate.
[05:12] Samir Khan: any SLA on Dedicated?
[05:14] Jordan Myers: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on commitment level. details in the contract/pricing doc.
[05:21] Alex Chen: are there any common transcription or understanding issues with model outputs? joking aside, how do you protect against regressions when we upgrade models?
[05:29] Priya Patel: We have quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals against your test sets and alert on regressions.
[05:38] Maya Torres: For instrumentation, how do we trace a single user request through batching?
[05:44] Priya Patel: We expose trace IDs and per-token logs in the console and provide SDK hooks for passing request IDs; the runtime correlates spans across batching boundaries.
[05:54] Samir Khan: Good. what's the expected cost delta between hosted and Dedicated for 200k q/day?
[05:59] Jordan Myers: Hard to say without payload sizes; generally Dedicated yields lower per-token cost when sustained volume is high because of reserved capacity. we'll run the estimate once you provide sample sizes.
[06:10] Alex Chen: Ok let's talk about timeline: we want to be in a POC within two weeks. can you support that?
[06:15] Priya Patel: Yes, that aligns — quickstart today with free credits, and SE benchmark next week.
[06:20] Jordan Myers: I'll send a calendar invite for a 60-min POC kickoff with Priya and your team.
[06:24] [07:00 - conversation continues with technical clarifications, skipping forward]
[20:00] Priya Patel: technical note — for rerankers it's often beneficial to use a two-stage pipeline: cheap prefilter embeddings then rerank. this reduces end-to-end cost and lets you tune latency.
[20:12] Maya Torres: we currently do the prefilter but use an off-the-shelf model for rerank, might try quantization. any recommended quantization settings?
[20:19] Priya Patel: we'll include suggested quant profiles in the benchmark doc; per-model profiles differ but 4-bit q4 variants often give good tradeoffs.
[20:28] Alex Chen: For the POC, are there limits on sample size we can test? we want to run realistic traffic.
[20:34] Jordan Myers: We can provision dedicated capacity for the benchmark; we'll coordinate limits based on region and availability.
[20:39] Samir Khan: Also curious about fallback strategies if Dedicated is saturated during spikes.
[20:44] Priya Patel: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity based on policy. we can configure cost vs latency preferences.
[20:54] [25:00] Alex Chen: last few questions: do you support IP allowlists and private endpoints?
[25:06] Jordan Myers: Yes — VPC peering, private endpoints, and IP allow lists are supported for Dedicated/Private.
[25:12] Maya Torres: perfect.
[25:15] Samir Khan: ok i'm sold on doing the quickstart. what do we need to do right now?
[25:19] Jordan Myers: step 1: sign up and redeem free credits — I'll send the link. step 2: run the quick cURL example and confirm you can call the API. step 3: share sample payloads and target qps so Priya can run the benchmark.
[25:31] Alex Chen: we'll get that to you by end of week.
[25:33] Jordan Myers: great. i will follow up with pricing, SOC2/ISO docs, and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[25:40] Maya Torres: thanks — excited to try time-to-first-token.
[25:43] Jordan Myers: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with next steps in email and calendar.
